facts.text: MiniWorld-Maze-v0 is registered to the miniworld.envs.maze:Maze class
Maze restricts the action space to Discrete(move_forward + 1), the three movement actions
MiniWorldEnv numbers turn_left 0, turn_right 1 and move_forward 2 in its Actions enumeration
The default observation is a 60 by 80 RGB image with 3 channels
The observation space is Box(low=0, high=255, shape=(obs_height, obs_width, 3), dtype=uint8)
Every step renders a fresh observation from the agent camera
The base step truncates when step_count reaches max_episode_steps and reports reward 0 on that step
Maze defaults max_episode_steps to num_rows * num_cols * 24 and its default grid is 8 by 8
The sparse reward is 1.0 - 0.2 * (step_count / max_episode_steps)
Maze adds the sparse reward and sets termination when the agent is near the red box
The default movement parameters are forward_step 0.15, forward_drift 0 and turn_step 15, with randomization ranges 0.12-0.17, -0.05-0.05 and 10-20
Domain randomization is disabled by default (domain_rand=False)
reset takes the gymnasium seed parameter and options, seeds the random generator and rebuilds the agent, the entities and the rooms
Maze places the red Box and then the agent in the generated world
Motion is kinematic: move_agent and turn_agent change the agent position and direction directly and a move is rejected when intersect() reports a collision
The default Box size is 0.8 and its bounding radius is sqrt(sx * sx + sz * sz) / 2
The agent has a bounding radius of 0.4
near() compares the distance with both radii plus 1.1 * max_forward_step
The constructor opens a 1 by 1 hidden pyglet window and allocates frame buffers, so the real environment needs an OpenGL context
MiniWorld is a minimalistic 3D interior environment simulator for reinforcement learning and robotics research
The upstream lists its physics as very basic, not sufficient for robot arms or manipulation
The package requirements are Python >=3.8, numpy>=1.22.0, pyglet>=1.5.27,<2.0 and gymnasium>=0.29.1

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial pose and the dynamics are deterministic, so this package's fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws with Python's random.Random and upstream with gymnasium's numpy generator, so a seed does not reproduce an upstream trajectory

gaps: kinematic/analytic model: each action is a direct move or turn, with no rigid-body dynamics, contact solver, actuator, sensor or noise model (the upstream says its physics are very basic, README.md:43-45)
timestep_ms is 0 because the environment is event-driven: one action is one transition and there is no physics timestep; realtime_factor 0 means no wall-clock pacing

the fake backend does not generate the 8x8 room maze, walls or portals and has no collision detection; the agent moves on an open plane and the red box is placed 1.5 m ahead of it instead of in a random room (those values are test data, not device facts)
the fake returns a 3x4x3 coarse RGB stand-in (36 values) instead of the real 60x80x3 rendered camera image; there is no 3D rendering, texture, lighting or occlusion because pyglet/OpenGL is not used
initial poses come from Python's random.Random in the fake and from gymnasium's numpy generator upstream, so one seed does not reproduce an upstream trajectory
snapshot and restore are not offered: MiniWorldEnv exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
